We need to construct route using templates. We have many templates from search. The first result (reaction_id 20810) seems to be a disconnection of sulfonamide: product is sulfonamide attached to aromatic ring and an aniline with a side chain (the N-aryl sulfonamide). The reactants are a chlorosulfonyl aryl (Cl-SO2-Ar) and an aniline with side chain (the rest). That seems promising: break sulfonamide bond to give aryl sulfonyl chloride and an aniline.

Our target has sulfonamide linking a phenyl (with fluorophenyl) to an aniline (the rest). So we can disconnect to aryl sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-Ph-F) and the aniline (the rest). Then we need to synthesize each.

The aniline part: NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1

That's a phenyl ring with an amine (attached to sulfonyl) and a side chain: N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 (a dimethylamino? Actually N-alkyl piperazine? Wait N2CCN(... )CC2 is a morpholine? Actually N2CCN...CC2 is a N,N-dialkyl ethylenediamine? It's a N,N-dialkyl? It's a N,N-dialkyl? It's a N,N-dialkyl? It's a N,N-dialkyl? It's a N,N-dialkyl? But we can consider that the aniline part can be built via nucleophilic aromatic substitution? Or via coupling? Might be easier to consider that the aniline is a known building block: 4-((piperazin-1-yl)methyl)?? Actually N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 is a N-acylated piperazine? Wait piperazine is N1CCN(CC1). Here we have N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2: that's N-acyl piperazine with a t-butoxy carbonyl (Boc) group? C(OC(C)(C)C)=O is a tert-butyl carbonate? Actually C(OC(C)(C)C)=O is a carbamate (tert-butyl carbonate). So it's a piperazine bearing a carbamate.

Thus the aniline part could be derived from a simpler aniline (with amine) then attach piperazine via nucleophilic substitution? Actually the aniline has a substituent at position (maybe 4) that is N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 attached via nitrogen (i.e., anilide? Actually the SMILES: NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1

So the aniline nitrogen (the sulfonamide N) is attached to aromatic carbon (position 1). The aromatic ring also has a substituent N2CCN... attached directly to carbon (as an aniline substituent). So it's an aniline with a side chain containing a piperazine carbamate.

Thus we could disconnect that side chain via a C-N bond formation: maybe via Buchwald-Hartwig amination between aryl bromide and piperazine. So we need an aryl bromide (or chloride) precursor: the aromatic core with bromine at that position, and the piperazine carbamate as nucleophile.

Also the fused bicyclic part: C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3) is a bicyclic ring (maybe a tetrahydronaphthol). That could be derived from a simpler phenol via intramolecular cyclization? Might be commercially available as a building block.

Given time constraints, we can propose a plausible route using known commercial building blocks: 4-fluorophenylsulfonyl chloride (commercial), 4-bromo-2-... Actually the aryl sulfonyl chloride is Cl-SO2-Ph-F (para-fluoro). That's commercially available.

The aniline core: 4-(piperazin-1-yl)-2-(hydroxyl?) Actually the core includes a fused bicyclic ring (maybe a tetralol). Could be derived from 2-naphthol? The SMILES of core: C1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1. This looks like a naphthalene with a side chain.

Maybe we can use a known building block: 2-aminonaphthol? But with piperazine attached.

Given complexity, we can propose a route with 3 steps: 1) Couple piperazine carbamate to aryl bromide via Buchwald-Hartwig; 2) Form sulfonamide with aryl sulfonyl chloride; 3) Deprotect Boc to give final.
